The Spokesman of the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office of the State Council issued a statement on 2 July about a violent incident storming the Legislative Council in Hong Kong.
The statement expressed firm support to the HKSAR Government and the police in handling the incident in accordance with the law.
The statement said perpetrators of the violence would be investigated and held criminally responsible in accordance with the law.
The statement said that on July 1, some extremist radicals stormed the Legislative Council building in an extremely violent manner.
The statement said the radicals deliberately damaged the Legislative Council's facilities under the pretext of opposing the review of the law by the SAR government.
The statement said the offences trample on Hong Kong's rule of law, destroy Hong Kong's social order, and damage Hong Kong's fundamental interests.
The statement said the incident was a blatant challenge to the principle of "one country, two systems".
The statement said the Central Government resolutely supports the HKSAR Government and the police in discharging responsibilities in accordance with the law.
The statement said the Central Government supports HKSAR authorities in prosecuting criminal responsibility of perpetrators of violence in accordance with the law.
The statement said the goal was to restore normal social order as soon as possible, protect personal safety and property of citizens, and maintain prosperity and stability of Hong Kong.
Carrie Lam said she felt strong resentment and sadness at the extremely violent way some protesters stormed the Legislative Council on 1 July.
Carrie Lam strongly condemned the storming of the Legislative Council.
The Hong Kong SAR government will prosecute any illegal act to the end, according to Carrie Lam.
Some radicals in Hong Kong violently stormed and occupied the Legislative Council on the evening of July 1.
Hong Kong police cleared the area after midnight and drove out the protesters who had violently stormed and occupied the LegCo building.
Carrie Lam said that around 4 am on July 2, some protesters had been confronting police since the morning of July 1, blocking roads and attacking police officers with unknown liquids.
Carrie Lam said that at noon on July 2, the situation worsened with protesters storming the Legislative Council building using iron bars and shopping carts to smash the glass facade.
Carrie Lam said protesters brought toxic chemical powder to attack police.
Carrie Lam said that in the evening, protesters entered the Legislative Council building and destroyed the Chamber and the Hong Kong SAR emblem.
Carrie Lam said the lawless acts of violence seriously disrupted the core value of the rule of law in Hong Kong.
Carrie Lam said the police showed restraint in dealing with the violence throughout the day.
Carrie Lam said any violations of the law will definitely be pursued to the end.
On 2 July, Hong Kong media unanimously condemned the violent storming of the Legislative Council.
The media said the violence seriously violated the rule of law in Hong Kong.
The media called for strict punishment of the thugs without tolerance to reshape the environment of the rule of law and restore a peaceful environment to the people of Hong Kong.
An editorial in Ta Kung Pao stated that a "peaceful and rational" movement incited riots in collaboration with trouble-making local politicians and foreign powers.
The Ta Kung Pao editorial described the movement as a "bloody and violent" anti-government movement.
The Ta Kung Pao editorial called on Hong Kong citizens to stand together and give the police full support to punish the thugs severely.
The Ta Kung Pao editorial called for exposing "black hands" who manipulate from behind the scenes.
The Hong Kong Commercial Daily editorial said the demonstration turned into a violent and extreme attack that damaged public facilities, security, and stability.
The Hong Kong Commercial Daily editorial said the attack damaged Hong Kong's core values and spirit and harmed Hong Kong's reputation and image internationally.
An editorial in Sing Tao Daily said the majority of Hong Kong citizens yearn for peace and stability.
The Sing Tao Daily editorial said the behaviour of violent extremists works against that wish.
The Sing Tao Daily editorial called for all sectors to curb the frenzy and bring society back on track.
The Sing Tao Daily editorial said members of parliament, organizations from all sectors, and the public must clearly say "no" to violence.
The Sing Tao Daily editorial warned not to let violence worsen, especially among young people, to avoid exacerbating social unrest and damaging Hong Kong's future.
An editorial in Ming Pao titled "Violence is violence" said "violence against the Legislative Council must be condemned most severely".
The Ming Pao editorial said Hong Kong is still free and open and most Hong Kong people are peaceful, rational, and non-violent.
The Ming Pao editorial said society must draw a clear line against violence and must not take a conciliatory attitude.
The Ming Pao editorial said if violence is tolerated, it will continue to spread and become more serious.
Hong Kong public opinion generally believes Hong Kong's achievements are hard-won and the result of hard work and construction by all Hong Kong citizens.
Hong Kong public opinion said violence should not be allowed to destroy Hong Kong's values, rule of law, and order.
Hong Kong public opinion called on the whole society to put aside differences and work together to protect Hong Kong's achievements and beauty and create a better future.
